Runtime on sandboxed builds (hse keys against a scratch HOME, and a sandboxed hse serve for the console's pool routes): 0 of 10 checks before, 10 of 10 after (two unusable files in turn, a directory at .bak, every backup name taken, and the console's add, rotate and revoke over a pool that cannot be saved); with one backup name freed by hand, the next hse keys command moved the file there and a key added then persisted across processes. completed.contract: A settings.json that exists and cannot be read or parsed stops every hse command that reads a switch with the file and the fix, is never written over, and a toggle write keeps switches set in the file since the process loaded it (REQ-SETTINGS-001)
completed.evidence: Found: util::settings read the file with .ok()…unwrap_or_default(), so a trailing comma read as no overrides, turning auto-update, the map-tile fetch and the live radar back on without a word, and the next hse config replaced the file with the one switch it set; hse serve's toggle write also wrote out its stale copy, undoing hse config run meanwhile. Runtime on sandboxed builds (hse config, hse scan, build-sha against a scratch HOME; a copied binary's hse serve for the toggle PUT, the update trigger and a restart): 3 of 19 checks before (the three controls), 19 of 19 after: hse config refuses and names the file and the fix, the file keeps its bytes, the self-update never runs on it, hse scan stops, build-sha still answers, the console's toggle is a 409 with the refused switch not in effect, the update is refused naming the file, a repaired file keeps a switch set meanwhile across a restart, and hse serve does not start on a broken file. Each build read the other's settings writes, every switch kept. Two independent reviews: the first found build-sha refused, the cache changed before a refused write, a lazily filled cache that read a broken file as defaults, missing field docs and a binary test that did not prove the order; the second found a rustfmt failure, a load/write race, a stale update timer and a CHANGELOG line that said installs were unaffected. All fixed, and the nits but one (the guard runs once, before the install). Mutations: 20 of 20 caught, each applied alone; S14 (the apply_update guard removed) by the runtime check alone, from a copied binary outside any source tree.

competitors.name: SpiderFoot 4.0
competitors.why_same_shape: MIT, self-hosted Python OSINT automation with an embedded local web UI (sf.py -l) and CLIs (sf.py, sfcli.py) over a SQLite back-end. It takes the same all-source seeds (IP, domain, email, phone, username, name, bitcoin), and HSE explicitly reproduces its command surface and scan model (README.md:8-9, 336-359).

competitors.name: Recon-ng
competitors.why_same_shape: GPLv3, self-hosted Python recon framework with an interactive CLI, recon-cli, and recon-web (a local web UI plus REST API) over per-workspace SQLite. It serves the same web-based OSINT recon operators on Linux.

competitors.name: theHarvester
competitors.why_same_shape: GPLv2, self-hosted Python OSINT collector with a CLI, the HarvestView local web UI and a REST API on 127.0.0.1:5000, over a local SQLite evidence store. It overlaps HSE's domain, email, IP and breach sources and its authorised-use stance.

competitors.name: Maigret
competitors.why_same_shape: MIT, self-hosted Python person-OSINT tool that builds a dossier from a username and searches recursively on the IDs it finds. It has a CLI and a built-in local web UI (--web) and installs via pip or snap (amd64/arm64) on Linux. It covers HSE's username and identity slice.

competitors.name: OWASP Amass
competitors.why_same_shape: Apache-2.0 single static Go binary: a CLI with a local collection engine and asset DB for domain, IP and ASN mapping, the NETINT slice HSE also scans (README.md:371-374). Kept although it has no web UI, because its CLI, engine and output functions (viz, track, blacklists, -dir) overlap HSE's.
